advice: Propose one panel32 wrapper change: replace the n=512 call to `sera_libxsmm_512(parameters)` with a loop over `r=0,32,...,480` that calls the supplied `sera_libxsmm_panel32` once per row band. For each call set only `parameters[4]=B`, `parameters[10]=A+(size_t)r*512`, and `parameters[16]=C+(size_t)r*512`; keep other parameter slots zero. The helper computes 32 rows across all 512 columns and the full k reduction, so these disjoint bands cover every output row. This tests the legal row-panel loop order and the helper’s smaller packing footprint against the added call and SME transition overhead. It is a distinct feasible wrapper change, but it was already measured in the supplied history in Low Power and Automatic modes; both outcomes were unpromoted. Do not repeat it as a new experiment. I have no other distinct, source-supported loop-order change to recommend from the supplied evidence.
risks: Do not claim a speedup or infer a cache cause from the prior noisy scores. A new loop order using the existing full512 body would require coordinated edits to its packed-A setup, consumer strides, B/C traversal, and rewinds; the evidence does not establish a useful new variant. The proposed helper loop must preserve the exact pointer mapping and zero all unused parameter fields. Check full GEMM correctness at n=512, general sizes and tails, n<=0 behavior, output overwrite, ABI and license notices. Any genuinely new source needs fresh paired measurements under the fixed hill and unchanged power settings; retain AC and battery evidence separately.
